item.title: Cryptography 11: From Lindner–Peikert to Kyber — Building the Module-LWE Key Encapsulation Mechanism
item.description: This post traces the path from the Lindner–Peikert cryptosystem — an early LWE-based encryption scheme with provable correctness and CPA security — through the polynomial ring underlying lattice cryptography, where multiplication turns into a structured matrix operation and coefficient sizes stay tightly controlled, to Module-LWE (MLWE), a generalization of LWE that remains as hard as ordinary LWE despite its extra structure. Building on MLWE, Kyber-PKE achieves an extremely low decryption failure rate and provable CPA security, and after ciphertext compression per the FIPS 203 standard, is upgraded via the Fujisaki–Okamoto transform into Kyber-KEM (ML-KEM) — NIST’s standardized, chosen-ciphertext-secure, plaintext-aware key encapsulation mechanism.
